newsitem.title: USA: Privatization growing among Illinois governments.
newsitem.headline: Privatization growing among Illinois governments.

text.p: Nearly one-fifth of Illinois municipalities plan to expand privatization efforts in the future, according to a report released Thursday.

The report by the Illinois comptroller's office, the Illinois Institute for Rural Affairs at Western Illinois University and the Illinois Municipal League, indicated that almost all municipalities have contracted for at least one service, with solid waste collection and disposal being the most common services.

The report, which was based on a survey of more than 500 municipalities, also found that more than 40 percent of cities with populations of at least 5,000 plan to increase contracting in areas such as water treatment, distribution and sewage collection.

About two-thirds of the municipalities surveyed reported successful privatization in most cases, while 15.1 percent called it a success in some cases. Only 1.3 percent of the respondants said privatization failed in most cases.

"Privatization is working in many instances and saving taxpayers money while maintaining current services. That is the bottom line," said Kenneth Alderson, executive director of the municipal league, in a news release.
